vectors.description: IDFA/IDFV, sysctl hardware probes, boot time, disk space, carrier data.
vectors.title: Device & environment fingerprinting
vectors.userAdvice: Limit fingerprinting: Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Tracking ▸ turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track". Fingerprints can survive resets, so favour apps that don't do it.

vectors.description: CoreLocation use, especially background or significant-change monitoring.
vectors.title: Location tracking
vectors.userAdvice: Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Location Services ▸ [app]: choose "While Using" or "Never", and turn OFF "Precise Location" if exact position isn't needed. Avoid granting "Always".

vectors.description: Pasteboard reads, contacts/photo library access, calendar/reminders access.
vectors.title: Content access (clipboard / contacts / photos / calendar)
vectors.userAdvice: Grant Photos and Contacts as "Limited"/"Selected" rather than full access (Settings ▸ Privacy). iOS warns when an app reads your clipboard. Decline paste prompts you didn't expect.

vectors.description: Touch event capture, accelerometer/gyroscope motion fingerprinting.
vectors.title: Behavioural biometrics & motion sensors
vectors.userAdvice: Motion and touch profiling can't be toggled per-app; restrict Motion & Fitness in Settings ▸ Privacy where offered, and prefer apps that disclose this behaviour.

vectors.description: Camera/mic capture, screen-recording detection or capture.
vectors.title: Audio / video / screen capture
vectors.userAdvice: Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Camera / Microphone: disable for apps that don't need them. The orange (mic) and green (camera) dots show active use. Watch for unexpected activations.

vectors.description: Probing which other apps are installed via URL schemes / canOpenURL / LSApplicationQueriesSchemes.
vectors.title: Installed-app enumeration
vectors.userAdvice: Not user-controllable. An app probing which other apps you have installed is profiling you. Prefer alternatives with clearer privacy practices and review the developer's privacy policy.

vectors.description: BLE scanning, UWB ranging, Wi-Fi/BSSID info, Bonjour service enumeration and retail-beacon SDKs. Fingerprints the user's physical and household environment (who/what is nearby).
vectors.title: Proximity & cross-device sensing
vectors.userAdvice: This app can sense nearby devices (Bluetooth/UWB/Wi-Fi), building a picture of your physical surroundings. In Settings ▸ Privacy, deny Bluetooth and Local Network access to apps that don't clearly need them.

vectors.description: Known analytics/anti-fraud SDKs that ship device + behaviour data off-device.
vectors.title: Analytics / attribution / anti-fraud SDKs
vectors.userAdvice: Turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track" and review any in-app analytics/personalisation toggles. A filtering DNS profile can further cut telemetry.

vectors.description: X-Mode / Anomaly Six / Outlogic / Babel Street / SafeGraph / Vermillion / Predicio / Cuebiq: location and behaviour brokers.
vectors.title: Data-broker embedding
vectors.userAdvice: Strong privacy red flag. Opt out of tracking (Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Tracking) and, where available, the data broker's own opt-out page; consider removing the app.

vectors.description: Where data egresses. Endpoint geography and owner are inferred statically from URLs, as a data-residency and cross-border transfer signal.
vectors.title: Server region / data residency
vectors.userAdvice: Your data may be sent to servers in other countries with different privacy laws. Review the privacy policy before sharing sensitive information.

vectors.description: LLM/vision/speech SDKs and cloud AI endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, Azure OpenAI, cloud STT) that send free-text user content (messages, photos, screen context) off the device.
vectors.title: AI / LLM data egress
vectors.userAdvice: This app can send what you type, say or photograph to a cloud AI service. Avoid sharing sensitive personal, health or financial details in its AI features, and review the privacy policy for how prompts are retained.

vectors.description: Apple-mandated API category is used inside binaries but not declared in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. An App Store policy violation.
vectors.title: Privacy-manifest gap (used vs declared)
vectors.userAdvice: A disclosure/compliance gap rather than a user control. Treat undisclosed data use as a caution sign when deciding whether to trust the app.

vectors.description: Tracking capability (IDFA / tracking SDKs) present alongside App Tracking Transparency. Flags collection that may precede or bypass user consent.
vectors.title: Consent / ATT ordering integrity
vectors.userAdvice: If the app tracks you before you tap "Ask App Not to Track", that's a consent red flag. Turn off Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Tracking ▸ "Allow Apps to Request to Track".

vectors.description: Kids-genre apps embedding ad trackers, absent age-gate/Declared-Age-Range signals, and SDK COPPA/child-directed flags. A kids-facing app with ad trackers is a different and worse finding than the same SDK elsewhere.
vectors.title: Child-safety & age-assurance signals
vectors.userAdvice: If this is a child-facing app, embedded ad/tracking SDKs are a serious concern. Prefer apps in the Kids category that state they don't use third-party advertising, and set up Screen Time / Ask to Buy for children.

vectors.description: Checks for VPN tunnels and proxy settings.
vectors.title: VPN / proxy detection
vectors.userAdvice: If you use a VPN or privacy tool, be aware this app can detect it and may change behaviour or block you. No user setting disables this detection.

vectors.description: Frida / Cydia / debugger / dyld checks and ptrace tricks used to resist analysis.
vectors.title: Anti-analysis / anti-debug / anti-jailbreak
vectors.userAdvice: Usually defensive (anti-fraud / anti-tamper). If the app refuses to run on your device for no clear reason, this is often why. No user action needed.

vectors.description: Background URL sessions, BGTaskScheduler, expiring background tasks used for telemetry drain.
vectors.title: Hidden background exfiltration
vectors.userAdvice: Reduce silent background data sends: Settings ▸ General ▸ Background App Refresh ▸ turn off for this app.

vectors.description: XOR-decoded interface names, runtime string decoding, suspicious constant tables.
vectors.title: Obfuscation indicators
vectors.userAdvice: Heavy obfuscation isn't proof of wrongdoing but it hides behaviour; prefer apps that are transparent about what they collect and do.

vectors.description: Strings, domains, file paths and sandbox-escape primitives matching published commercial-spyware IOCs (Citizen Lab datasets).
vectors.title: Known spyware / stalkerware IOCs
vectors.userAdvice: Treat as serious. Don't log in, update iOS immediately, enable Lockdown Mode (Settings ▸ Privacy & Security), and seek expert help if you may be targeted.

vectors.description: App Transport Security weaknesses, cleartext HTTP exceptions, weak TLS, and missing certificate pinning markers.
vectors.title: Transport security (ATS / TLS / pinning)
vectors.userAdvice: On untrusted Wi-Fi, apps with weak transport security can leak data. Avoid sensitive actions on public networks when using such apps.

vectors.description: World-readable files, plaintext databases, NSFileProtectionNone, and Keychain misuse markers.
vectors.title: Data-at-rest protection
vectors.userAdvice: Set a device passcode and enable Face/Touch ID (this turns on file data protection), and avoid storing sensitive information in apps flagged here.

vectors.description: Weak primitives (DES, MD5, RC4), ECB mode, hardcoded keys/certs, custom XOR. Compliance and trust risk.
vectors.title: Cryptography
vectors.userAdvice: Nothing to toggle; weak cryptography is a developer issue. Avoid storing highly sensitive data in apps that show crypto warnings.

vectors.description: PIE/ASLR, stack canaries, ARC, and encryption state of each Mach-O binary.
vectors.title: Binary hardening
vectors.userAdvice: Developer-side hardening. Weak hardening slightly raises exploit risk, so keep iOS and the app updated.

vectors.description: API keys, tokens, private keys and other high-entropy secrets embedded in binaries or resources.
vectors.title: Hardcoded secrets & credentials
vectors.userAdvice: Developer issue with no direct user action, but embedded keys signal weaker security hygiene. Be cautious with sensitive data in this app.

vectors.description: Enterprise / ad-hoc / development profiles, expired signing and sideload markers, relevant for non-App-Store distribution.
vectors.title: Code signing / entitlement posture
vectors.userAdvice: If this app isn't from the App Store, only install it from a source you fully trust. Sideloaded and enterprise apps bypass App Store review.

vectors.description: Keychain items stored without an access-control / accessibility class and biometric/passcode policy use: the strength of credential storage and local auth.
vectors.title: Authentication & keychain protection
vectors.userAdvice: Set a strong device passcode and enable biometrics; both strengthen how the app's stored credentials are protected.

vectors.description: Third-party SDK provenance and update/CDN channel: embedded trackers and their owner class as a software-supply-chain risk.
vectors.title: SDK provenance & supply chain
vectors.userAdvice: Bundled third-party SDKs widen who gets your data and the app's supply-chain risk. Prefer apps with fewer embedded trackers; keep the app updated.

vectors.description: The iOS versions the app still supports and the SDK and Xcode it was built with.
vectors.title: Platform version
vectors.userAdvice: Keep iOS and the app up to date. An app that still runs on old iOS versions cannot rely on protections Apple added since.

vectors.description: WKWebView, JS evaluation bridges, message handlers, JS-injected scripts: a common channel for credential and UA exfiltration.
vectors.title: WebView / JavaScript bridge
vectors.userAdvice: Avoid typing passwords on in-app web screens. Open sensitive links in Safari instead, where you can verify the address bar.

vectors.description: Custom URL schemes the app itself registers (CFBundleURLSchemes) and wildcard universal-link domains: inbound attack surface where unvalidated parameters can drive sensitive actions.
vectors.title: Deep-link / URL-scheme handler exposure
vectors.userAdvice: Be wary of links that open this app from messages or websites; don't tap deep links from untrusted sources.

vectors.description: Bundled app extensions (PlugIns/*.appex): custom keyboards with RequestsOpenAccess (keystroke exfiltration) and share/action extensions with TRUEPREDICATE activation rules.
vectors.title: App extensions & custom keyboards
vectors.userAdvice: For a bundled custom keyboard, deny "Full Access" (Settings ▸ General ▸ Keyboard) unless you truly need it. Full access can send keystrokes off your device.

vectors.description: Background-execution and remote-wakeup surface: UIBackgroundModes abuse, VoIP/background processing, and silent / VoIP / critical push. These wake the app without user awareness.
vectors.title: Background-activation surface
vectors.userAdvice: Limit how the app wakes itself: turn off Background App Refresh and revoke unused Location/Notification permissions in Settings.
